items.headline: Tech Sector Drags Down Major Indices; Strong Earnings Boost Health Stocks Amidst Fed's Steady Rate Stance
items.summary: U.S. equities closed mostly lower on Thursday, primarily driven by a significant sell-off in the technology sector following disappointing earnings from Alphabet. Despite this, positive earnings from companies like Eli Lilly bolstered health care stocks. The Federal Reserve's decision yesterday to hold interest rates steady, along with robust Q3 GDP data, provided some underlying support, but inflation concerns remain present.

items.headline: Eli Lilly Surges on Raised Outlook
items.summary: Eli Lilly ($LLY) climbed 7.25% to $1378.08 after its third-quarter results showed revenue growth of 39% driven by its Mounjaro and Zepbound drugs, prompting a raised 2026 revenue forecast to $91 billion-$92 billion.

items.headline: Crocs Jumps on Strong Q3 and Upbeat Forecast
items.summary: Crocs ($CROX) shares surged 25.54% following robust third-quarter 2026 financial results and a raised full-year outlook. The company reported consolidated revenues up 4.6% and its HEYDUDE brand returned to growth.

items.headline: Alphabet Plummets on Disappointing Earnings and AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: Alphabet ($GOOGL) shares tumbled 12.64% after reporting weaker third-quarter growth, missing Wall Street's revenue and profit expectations, and posting negative free cash flow due to substantial AI capital spending. The decline erased approximately $500 billion of its market value.

items.headline: Xerox Falls Sharply on Cut Forecasts
items.summary: Xerox ($XRX) dropped 40.32% after cutting its full-year forecasts, overshadowing its third-quarter results.

items.headline: Fortinet Declines on Service Revenue Forecast Cut
items.summary: Fortinet ($FTNT) fell 20.09% following its third-quarter results, where it cut its forecast for service revenue despite raising its overall 2026 revenue forecast. The stock also faced a downgrade from BofA.

items.headline: Healthcare and Financials Lead as Tech and Communication Services Lag
items.summary: Today's market saw a clear rotation, with the Healthcare sector leading gains, rising 2.06%, and Financials also performing strongly with a 1.7% increase. In contrast, the Communication Services sector lagged significantly, falling 1.91%, and Technology was down 1.37%, largely due to major earnings disappointments within the sector.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady, Eyes December Hike Amidst Inflation Concerns
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate target range at 3.75%-4.00% during its October meeting, with a 10-2 vote. Two members dissented, favoring a quarter-point hike due to persistent inflation. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh indicated that while economic activity is strong, inflation remains elevated, suggesting a data-dependent approach for a potential December rate hike.

items.headline: U.S. Economy Accelerates with 3.4% GDP Growth in Q3
items.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026, an acceleration from the 2.2% growth in the second quarter. This robust expansion was primarily driven by increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending.

items.headline: Amazon and Intel Decline in After-Hours Trading on Earnings
items.summary: Following the market close, both Amazon ($AMZN) and Intel ($INTC) saw their shares fall in after-hours trading after releasing their respective earnings reports. Intel declined 17.60% after forecasting less revenue for the fourth quarter than the third, while Amazon also experienced a drop.
